newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK SAYS LOWER M2 GROWTH MAIN '97 GOAL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK SAYS LOWER M2 GROWTH MAIN '97 GOAL.

text.p: Czech central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky on Thursday said a reduction of the growth of the key money measure, M2, was the main goal for the central bank's monetary policy in 1997.
"The main goal (for 1997 monetary policy) is a reduction in the money supply as measured by the M2 aggregate," Tosovksy told a news conference.
Czech M2 measures currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits.
Tosovsky also restated the central bank's target for 1997 M2 growth, which was released last week, saying growth of between eight and 12 percent in the money supply was the target for the year.
The central bank's target for 1996 M2 growth was between 13 and 17 percent.

Earlier on Thursday the central bank released figures showing M2 growth to the end of November had eased to 9.7 percent, year-on-year, from 9.8 percent in October. In November 1995, M2 year-on-year growth was 22.1 percent.

Tosovksy the aim of having average inflation 7.9 percent for 1997, which the central bank also released last week, was condidtioned on the government's resolution of regulated prices and on the deregulation of prices.
It also depends on a reduction in the growth of real wages, he added.
He said getting real wage growth down to "around 13 percent" from the current level of between 17-18 percent "would certainly help".
